newsitem.title: ITALY: FAO sees '96 world cereal output at 1.849 bln T.
newsitem.headline: FAO sees '96 world cereal output at 1.849 bln T.

text.p: The U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said on Monday that its latest forecast for 1996 world cereal production was 1.849 billion tonnes.
The Rome-based organisation said in a special outlook released in connection with this week's world food summit that the figure was 6.9 percent up from 1995's level.
It was also higher than FAO's last forecast in September which put world production at 1.821 billion tonnes.
"The outlook for global food supplies in 1996/97 has improved somewhat since the last report," FAO said.

"With most of the world's 1996 cereal crops already harvested or about to be gathered, FAO's forecast of global production has become more firm and now indicates a larger recovery from 1995 than earlier expected."

The agency said latest information on 1996 crops pointed to larger increases in global wheat and coarse grains output than expected while rice production was forecast to rise significantly from last year.
"The bulk of the increase in cereal output is forecast in wheat and coarse grains production in the developed countries," FAO said.
However, it warned that the outcome of the 1996 cereal harvest could still be affected by adverse weather in the coming weeks.
